nodes.label: Lesson 01 — Race conditions: who wins, and who loses silently
The lost update (measured: -400 discrepancy)
nodes.rationale: Five actors withdrawing 100 each from a 100 balance are all approved; the balance reads 0 while 500 left the bank. Every line of the naive read-think-write is defensible — no null check missing, no off-by-one — which is why reviewers approve it.

nodes.label: Silent losers
nodes.rationale: Unlike an ordinary bug, the symptom is a success response: nothing throws, nothing logs, every customer gets 200 OK. Found by an auditor months later rather than by tests. Detection in production needs invariants — a reconciliation job asserting the sum of transactions equals the balance delta; if you can't state your invariant you can't detect its violation.

nodes.label: The sawVer column — every actor read version 1
nodes.rationale: The whole bug in one column of the recorded timeline: three actors each computed 100 - 40 = 60 from the same stale snapshot and each wrote 60. The final version descends from version 1, so the intervening versions and the withdrawals they represented were erased with no error anywhere.

nodes.label: RunSummaryCalculator
nodes.rationale: Decides who won by replaying writes against the version each actor read, not by comparing balances (two actors can write the same value). Works unchanged for the in-memory counter and for Postgres xmin, because it only needs versions to be unique, never ordered.

nodes.label: forceRace parameter
nodes.rationale: Makes the interleaving a parameter instead of an accident: gate.ReachAsync at InterleaveCheckpoints.AfterRead is a no-op dictionary lookup in production and a barrier in a forced run, so the lost update happens 100% of the time and a test asserts it across 25 consecutive runs. A test that catches a bug one run in twenty is a flaky test, and flaky tests get muted.

nodes.label: Why tests don't catch it — the test is the only user
nodes.rationale: WithoutContention_TheNaiveVersionIsPerfectlyCorrect passes, and so does the integration test and QA, because the bug needs a second actor to arrive during the gap and in testing there is rarely a second actor.

nodes.label: The naive handler is correct for a single writer
nodes.rationale: Simplest and fastest — no locks, no retries, no round-trips — and genuinely right where an account is only ever written by one process in one place, such as a single-consumer queue. What makes it unacceptable for money is that it fails silently, and silent corruption is worse than a crash.
